Ghanaian dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has urged young people involved in hard drug use to quit, warning that substance abuse could undermine their health and future prospects.
He said the future should be centred on healthy living, personal growth, collective development and wealth creation rather than the use of substances that could lead to addiction and rehabilitation.
Speaking in an interview on Afternoon Ride with Andy Dosty on Hitz FM, the musician said reports of people being taken to rehabilitation centres and, in some cases, sent to villages to recover from substance abuse had become a source of concern to him.
He said he wanted to use his influence to caution his fans and the wider youth population against hard drugs.
“I have always been trying to keep it up. The stories I am hearing with the people we are paying monies to, people going to rehab, some of them we have to take them to the village,” he said.
Shatta Wale stressed that young people should not mistake drug use for a pathway to success, arguing that the country's future depended on a generation that prioritised its health while working towards economic prosperity.
“I am like, let me just echo this out there for all my fans, for every youth out there, that that is not the future. The future is us building and growing together healthy and then getting wealth,” he added.
He also cautioned against individuals who encourage others to take substances, describing such influence as problematic.
While acknowledging that people may choose to get high, the artiste urged young people to draw a distinction between that and the use of hard drugs.
He further appealed directly to those already involved in hard drug use to reconsider their choices and seek to stop.
“Anywhere people have seen Shatta Wale, I just want to echo into the minds of every youth that if you are into hard drugs, I will urge you to stop,” he said.
